program.notes: ORE V3 (regolith-labs/ore), a Steel-framework program (no Anchor IDL — seeds live in source). Singletons config/board/treasury are const-only; automation/miner bind `authority`, which is NOT always the tx signer — claimOre/claimSol seed miner by the SIGNER and assert miner.authority == signer, while deploy/checkpoint take a SEPARATE authority account and seed miner by IT. The claim flow is wired (plan_claim -> claimOre): 11 accounts, payout in ORE base units at ELEVEN decimals, recipient is the signer's ORE ATA which the PROGRAM creates if empty (no prelude needed), and treasury_tokens is the treasury PDA's ATA (a two-step derivation no surface expresses). Two live comprehension gaps, both measured: (1) claimOre carries an OPTIONAL `bps` arg in source (ClaimORE { bps: [u8;8] }; omitted data = 100%) that the shipped idl.json and Orquestra both declare as args:[] — /build returns data '04' even when bps is passed, so a partial-claim ask silently becomes a full claim; 6 of the last 7 real mainnet claimOre instructions carried that arg. (2) checkpoint — claim's precondition — takes 8 accounts on mainnet (193/193 sampled) including the separate `authority` + `automation`, but the surface declares 6. The `stake` account is CPI'd across a program boundary and belongs to the SEPARATE ore-stake program — its owner is stakecNP..., not ORE. Naming gotcha (wire-verified): this Orquestra project speaks camelCase account AND instruction names (claimOre, treasuryTokens, oreProgram) — unlike the pump/meteora projects' snake_case. Recipes cross-verified against regolith-labs/ore@master + real mainnet accounts.
